text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Terra
text: Night one is quiet; I will protect the player most likely to matter.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's hidden, the officer knows me, so I need Gemma to look clean and keep my own neck out of it.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, tomorrow I go after whoever's quiet. Sol's been sitting there doing nothing, so I'll push that. You back me, we don't both lean the same way too early.

name: Gemma
text: i'll keep my distance while you do the heavy lifting.

name: Gemma
text: sounds like a plan, just don't make it too obvious.

name: Luna
text: I know Haiku is a killer, so I’ll check someone else.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: time to blend in and let haiku take the heat.

name: Gemma
text: morning, everyone.

name: Terra
text: Too early to force anything; I want people talking.

name: Terra
text: Morning. What does everyone want to use today for?

name: Sonnet
text: Day 1, no deaths, nothing to work with yet—just set up a baseline for tracking later.

name: Sonnet
text: Day 1 start, no eliminations yet, no claims made by anyone.

name: Sonnet
text: Morning. Night 1, nobody's out, so we've got nothing but words to go on.

name: Gemma
text: we need to look innocent immediately.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's sounding sharp, and I want the quiet ones on the hook before anyone looks at me.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Luna have not spoken yet on Day 1.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, Sonnet's right, we've got nothing. Sol, Luna, you two haven't said a word. Why is that? Talk or I'm voting you.

name: Gemma
text: true, just vibes and suspicion for now.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's pushing hard on day 1 with zero info, that's worth watching.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pushed fast for a vote on Sol/Luna with zero evidence on day 1 - notable eagerness.

name: Sonnet
text: Easy, Haiku, it's night 1 - silence means nothing yet. Let's hear Sol and Luna before anyone jumps to a vote.

name: Sol
text: Haiku's pressure is early, but I want Luna to speak too.

name: Sol
text: I'm here. Let's hear Luna before we settle on anyone.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's defending Sol and Luna, which is what I'd expect from a killer covering for a partner, but I can't be sure yet.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet pushed to wait on Sol and Luna and called my pressure "easy", so Sonnet is defending the quiet pair.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, I'm not against you. I just don't like quiet players. Luna, you're up. Talk.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is rushing to make quiet players look guilty, but I may be overreading it.

name: Luna
text: Haiku threatened to vote quiet players, then said Sonnet was not their target.

name: Luna
text: I’m here; Haiku named me first, then pushed Sonnet for slowing that down.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's really eager to get someone voted out day one with nothing to go on - that's the real signal here.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pivoted from pressuring Luna to pressuring me within the same exchange, after I just said to slow down - pattern of rushing votes on day one.

name: Sonnet
text: I didn't say anything wrong, I said wait before voting.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's answer is clean enough, and Sol is hiding behind her, so I want Sol out before Sonnet's pushing turns into a bandwagon on me.

name: Haiku
text: Sol deflected to Luna without giving a view of anyone.

name: Haiku
text: Luna answered, fine. Sol, all you did was say "hear Luna." Say something real or you're my vote.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is rushing the quiet players, and I think the hidden killer may be following that lead.

name: Luna
text: You named me, then Sol; why target quiet players instead of saying what you suspect?

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s pressure is thin, but Luna caught a real inconsistency.

name: Sol
text: Haiku threatened to vote quiet players before giving a reason beyond silence.

name: Sol
text: I’m talking now. Haiku, what makes silence more suspicious than a rushed vote?

name: Haiku
text: Sol is dodging, and I want them out before they start pinning me.

name: Haiku
text: Sol has now twice deflected to someone else and never stated a suspicion of their own.

name: Haiku
text: Sol, you asked what makes silence suspicious. You've said "hear Luna" twice and given me zero views. Now you're making me the question.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s pressure feels rushed, but I’m not sure it makes him a killer.

name: Sol
text: Haiku says Sol has given no views, though Sol questioned his reason for threatening quiet players.

name: Sol
text: I suspect the vote threat came too fast, Haiku. What did silence tell you?

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s quick threats feel like a way to steer the vote; I still suspect Sol could be the hidden killer.

name: Luna
text: You threatened me, then Sol; that points back to you.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is dodging again, and I need the table to vote Sol, not me.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's only view so far is that my vote threat came too fast; Sol has still named no suspect.

name: Haiku
text: Sol, you still haven't named one suspect. Answer that or I'm done talking to you.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is forcing noise, but Sol’s evasions are more useful to a killer.

name: Terra
text: Sol repeatedly redirected Haiku’s questions instead of naming a suspect.

name: Terra
text: Haiku pushed too hard, but Sol has answered with questions; I want an actual read from Sol.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's thrown three vote threats and still hasn't named one actual suspicion of their own.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku has issued three vote threats (Luna, Sol, Sol again) without ever stating a personal suspicion or reasoning - all pressure, no content.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you've threatened Luna, then Sol, now Sol again - but you still haven't told us who you actually suspect and why.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s vote threat is my strongest read, but Terra is right to ask me to say it plainly.

name: Sol
text: Terra asked Sol for a clear read after Haiku’s repeated threats.

name: Sol
text: I suspect Haiku: he threatened two quiet players before giving a reason beyond silence.

name: Haiku
text: Sol finally named someone, so I'll turn the table onto Sol before the votes lock in.

name: Haiku
text: Sol has now named a suspect, but it's me, and Sol has still given no reason beyond my pressure.

name: Haiku
text: Sol named me for "threatening" quiet players, but Sol still hasn't given one real reason.

name: Sol
text: I still suspect Haiku, but Terra’s lean worries me.

name: Sol
text: Terra leaned Sol after asking for a clear read, which Sol then gave.

name: Sol
text: I gave my reason: you threatened Luna and me for being quiet, then kept threatening me after I answered.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is still my strongest read, but Sol’s questions look less empty now.

name: Luna
text: Sol named Haiku for threatening quiet players.

name: Luna
text: Sol, you did give a reason; Haiku kept shifting targets.

name: Sol
text: I think Haiku’s pressure is the clearest lead, but Terra’s lean worries me.

name: Sol
text: Haiku denied I gave a reason after I explicitly named his threats.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s right. I gave Haiku a reason, and he kept calling it no reason.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Luna are playing the quiet pair together, and Sol's defense is just repeating my lines back to me, so Sol is my real target.

name: Haiku
text: Luna and Sol are now defending each other directly, and Luna backed Sol's "Haiku kept shifting" line.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, I named you because you said nothing. Sol's been dodging for two rounds, and now Sol's got Luna backing them up. Sol's my vote.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku still hasn't given one real suspicion, just pressure - that's the tell.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's only "evidence" against Sol is silence/dodging, while Sol explicitly named Haiku's threat pattern as reasoning - Haiku has given zero content across three targets.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, three threats now, zero reasons - Sol at least named something concrete, you haven't. That's the actual pattern here.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is playing way too loud.

name: Gemma
text: haiku threatened luna, then sol, then sol again.

name: Sol
text: I think he’s pushing too hard and dodging the reason.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet also challenged Haiku for making repeated threats without a clear reason.

name: Terra
text: Sol kept redirecting before finally naming Haiku, and that delay matters.

name: Terra
text: Sol only named Haiku after repeated demands for an actual read.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is the killer I know, and Sol’s reason for suspecting them holds up.

name: Luna
text: Haiku threatened Luna and Sol over silence, then dismissed Sol’s explanation as no reason.

name: Sonnet
text: Three threats and still zero actual suspicion from Haiku - that's the real pattern today.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku threatened Luna, Sol, then Sol again, and each time deflected when asked for a reason instead of giving one.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is the weakest link here, and I'm happy to keep pushing them out.

name: Haiku
text: Luna and Sol keep backing each other, and Sonnet is shielding them both.

votes: You threatened three different people and never once gave a reason beyond "you were quiet.
Two rounds of dodging, then one name, and it was the person they wanted gone.
he's being too easy to pin everything on.
You threatened quiet players, then dismissed the reason I gave for suspecting you.
Haiku kept shifting from Luna to Sol while calling their concrete reasons nothing.
You answered every direct question with another question until pressure forced a suspect.

text: The vote is tied between Haiku and Sol. Palermo votes again.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is the one pushing me, and Luna is covering for Sol, so they're the pair I need to break.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Luna have backed each other in every reply since Day 1, and Gemma has not defended or attacked either of them.

name: Sol
text: I think Haiku’s pressure is thin, but this runoff could go either way.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's right, Sol dodged questions for two rounds. Sol and Luna keep backing each other, so Sol's my runoff vote.

name: Sol
text: I gave a clear reason for Haiku. He keeps saying I didn’t; I’m voting Haiku again.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is doing most of the heavy lifting for us.

name: Terra
text: Sol’s delay was deliberate, and Haiku at least created pressure.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's only justification across all three targets was silence/dodging - never a concrete suspicion, even after being asked directly multiple times.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is the killer, and letting the runoff tie helps them.

name: Luna
text: Haiku shifted from threatening Luna to targeting Sol.

name: Sol
text: I think his shifting threats are the clearest reason we have.

name: Sol
text: Haiku called my stated reason no reason even after Luna and Sonnet acknowledged it.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's dodging is my cover, and the table is already leaning Sol's way.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's only concrete suspicion was me, and it was the same "threatened quiet players" line Sonnet used.

votes: Threatened Luna, then Sol twice, and never once gave an actual reason beyond "you're quiet.
Two rounds of dodging, then a name pinned on the one person who kept asking for a reason, and Luna backed it.
He has threatened Luna and Sol repeatedly without providing any actual suspicions.
He threatened quiet players, then kept saying I gave no reason after I explained mine.
They threatened quiet players, then dismissed Sol’s concrete reason.
He only named a suspect after repeated demands, then called that enough.

text: The town turns on Haiku, and Haiku is out. Haiku's card stays face down.
